subject.title: [Bug]: Managed Memory Dreaming Promotion cron silently NO_REPLY since 2026-05-09 (jobs.json lastRun stays null)

question: Should managed Dreaming cron treat per-workspace failures or zero-effect sweeps as cron errors/degraded status, or keep the cron run green and surface failures only through Dreaming diagnostics?
rationale: Current source supports both interpretations: the scheduler can record only the outer handled run, while memory-core has workspace-level failure information that users expect to see when diary output stops.

options.title: Surface degraded or error status
options.body: Make memory-core propagate failed-workspace or no-useful-work outcomes into a cron-visible error/degraded result with matching tests and doctor/status wording.

options.title: Keep cron green with stronger diagnostics
options.body: Leave cron success tied to the outer run and make Dreaming events, doctor/status, and docs the supported failure surface for per-workspace problems.

options.title: Close after fresh live proof
options.body: If maintainers believe current releases solve the user problem, request one latest-release live repro and close if no current failure remains.

recommendation.title: Surface degraded or error status
recommendation.body: Make memory-core propagate failed-workspace or no-useful-work outcomes into a cron-visible error/degraded result with matching tests and doctor/status wording.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the recent SQLite Dreaming-state fix and current cron/dreaming status changes nearest to this decision.
